scope: Native uncertainty occurrence preservation in ordinary save, load and correction workflows
environment: Linux, Python 3.12.14, installed rig test dependencies, repository root
command: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 PYTHONPATH=scripts:tests python -m unittest -v test_rig_uncertainty_occurrence_mutation

failed.test_direct_correction_preserves_opaque_: Native correction and reload succeeded. Actual observations contained only gripper. Expected gripper followed by the complete original pending jaw.left observation.
failed.test_equal_count_save_never_transfers_ow: Save, reload, dispatcher correction and final reload succeeded. Actual observations contained gripper and jaw.right. Expected the complete original pending jaw.left observation between them.

passed_controls.test_reordered_observations_cannot_reacq: After reversing the surviving left-jaw and gripper occurrences and appending a new observation, removing the bone retained the pending left-jaw record and preserved inventory order.
passed_controls.test_unaffected_fitted_observation_follo: Renaming the independently fitted gripper moved its pending observation. A later roll correction changed only that observation to corrected.

fixture: A local synthetic GLB is imported and fitted with the native robotic template and three omitted landmarks. A generic save introduces an independent copy of a fitted uncertainty. No test assigns or inspects ownership metadata. All four cases check original source and existing revision/correction files byte-for-byte across writes and reloads.

historical_evidence.scope: Those separately recorded 93 passing tests ran before the new four-test module existed. Their logs and the original four native probe outcomes remain bound to their original revisions.

evidence_level: Executed offline synthetic native Python workflows. The four-test run establishes the frozen failures and passing controls only. It does not verify a proposed fix, CI, artistic acceptance or completion of the parent issue.
